title: docmeta artifact-evals vocabulary (1.0.0-proposal.1)
description: Eval declarations for instruction artifacts — skills, agent definitions, and project-rules files: assertions about what must have held in an agent session that used the artifact. A docmeta common vocabulary sharing the entry shape of docmeta:evals:1.0.0-proposal.1: any session-grading tool can implement it. The page-side trio appears here one level down — `metadata.evals` (one assertion or the list), `metadata.eval-skip`, `metadata.eval-provenance` — because an artifact's top-level frontmatter is the host tool's contract and `metadata` is its sanctioned extension bag; there is no container object inside it — the list is the value. `metadata` stays open (other tools' members pass untouched) and entry objects are closed; consumers should reserve the `eval` prefix inside `metadata` and reject unrecognized `eval-*` members, the same loud-typo guard as the page side.

evals.description: The evals for this artifact: one AI-judged assertion as a string, or a non-empty list of entries — string shorthands, or closed objects with a required id. An empty list is not a declaration; an artifact with no evals omits the key.

eval-skip.description: Skip this artifact's evals entirely — reported as skipped, never silently ignored. The page-side key, one level down; default false.

eval-provenance.description: Attribution for machine-proposed evals, one entry per model (consumers merge by generated-by; the schema dedupes identical entries): which eval ids it proposed, at what confidence. A human deletes an entry once those evals are reviewed — the family provenance pattern, one level down.

metadata.description: The host tool's sanctioned extension bag, which is why this vocabulary lives one level down where the page-side docmeta:evals:1.0.0-proposal.1 sits at the root: an artifact's top level belongs to whatever runtime loads it, and `metadata` is the one place a third party may add keys without colliding with it. Open, unlike the eval entries inside it, because the bag is shared — other tools put their own keys here and must keep working.

generated-by.description: Model or agent that proposed the evals.

confidence.description: Per-eval model confidence, 0..1, keyed by the same kebab eval ids as `evals`.

provenanceEntry.description: One model's proposal: who generated it, which of these keys it wrote, and how sure it was. Closed, because the whole value of the trail is that a reviewer can read it at a glance and delete the entry once the fields are checked — an unrecognized key here would be an unretired claim nobody notices.

evalEntry.description: One eval: a string shorthand (an AI-judged assertion at error severity — the legitimately id-less form), or a closed object. Branched with if/then rather than oneOf so a fault inside the object form is reported once, against the key that is wrong.

id.description: Unique (per artifact) kebab-case identifier. Required on the object form — position-derived names orphan cached verdicts whenever entries move; if an eval is worth an object, it is worth a stable name.

assertion.description: What must have held in the session that used this artifact.

type.description: Whether this eval protects working behavior or probes a boundary.

grader.description: How the assertion is checked. A full open enum here — any kebab name is legal, validated by the registry — because no schema conditional switches on it, unlike the page side.

provider.description: Which configured inference provider or agent judges an `ai`-graded eval. Legal values are whatever the inference dependency supports, validated at run time; omit for the config default.

command.description: Command to execute for command-graded evals. {trace} is replaced with the session trace path — the artifact-side analog of the page side's {file} — and exit 0 (or `success-exit-codes`) is a pass. Omitting it is the generation contract: tooling generates a check script from the assertion, then writes `command` and `generated-assertion-hash` back. Legal only alongside `grader: command`.

success-exit-codes.description: Exit codes that count as a pass.

generated-assertion-hash.description: sha256 of the assertion when the check script was generated — written back alongside `command`, and never legal without it. A mismatch with the current assertion triggers regeneration.

options.description: Grader-specific options; validated by the grader at run time, deliberately outside this schema — a grader's options evolve on the grader's schedule.

severity.description: How hard a failure of this eval is. Defaults to error.

severity-map.description: Maps a tool grader's own severities onto eval severities. Meaningful only on `tool:*` evals — imported from the page side to keep the entry vocabularies congruent.

skip.description: Skip this eval without deleting it. Defaults to false.

evidence.description: Hint telling the judge where in the session to look.

pass.description: Trace content the judge should rule passing — one anchor or several.

fail.description: Trace content the judge should rule failing — one anchor or several.

examples.description: Anchor examples of passing and failing behavior for the judge — one or several each.

then.description: An entry carrying an executable command must say grader: command.
success-exit-codes and timeout-ms configure command execution, so they are legal only alongside grader: command — present, or generated later under the generation contract.

inlineEval.description: One eval on an artifact, judged against a session trace. Closed, so a typo is a finding rather than an eval that silently never runs. `assertion` is unconditional here, unlike the page side where a tool grader can be its own check: every trace is new, so there is nothing to compare against but the words.

evalType.description: `capability` probes a boundary and is expected to fail sometimes; `regression` protects behavior that already works. Reported, not enforced.

severity.description: Only error-severity failures fail the eval; warning and info report but pass. Default error — the string shorthand implies it.

grader.description: How the assertion is checked: the AI judge (`ai`); a human review queue (`human` — judged per session, since every trace is new, unlike the page side where a verdict persists until the page changes); an executable check over the trace (`command`); a deterministic session grader — `tool-usage`, `skill-invoked`, `file-access`, `turn-count`, `cost`, `regex`, `json-output`; or a `tool:<kebab>` integration, the page side's namespace, accepted here so one grader spelling ports across both eval vocabularies. Recommended values, not a closed list: any kebab name is legal and validated against the grader registry at run time, so a new grader never needs a schema version — the one cost is that a stale or misspelled grader name passes this schema and is rejected by the registry instead.

anchorList.description: One anchor example, or a non-empty list of them.
